previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, and a history of chronic abdominal pain was admitted for acute-on-chronic lower abdominal pain radiating to the back and legs. She presented with confusion and visual hallucinations, attributed to stopping lactulose, rifaximin, and risperidone. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, but cultures were negative. CT and ultrasound revealed possible gastritis, a fibroid uterus, and a mildly dilated bile duct without obstruction. She developed melena and hematochezia during admission; upper endoscopy and colonoscopy showed no active bleeding source, but diverticulosis was noted. She received one unit of PRBCs and underwent capsule endoscopy, which showed no active bleed. Her mental status improved with medication re-initiation. Antibiotics were continued empirically for abdominal pain linked to prior UTIs. She was discharged home with optimized liver and psychiatric medications and instructions to follow up on capsule endoscopy results and possible MRI for persistent hallucinations and visual changes.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo female with alcoholic hepatitis presents with acute on 
chronic abdominal pain and back pain, with abdomen tender to 
palpation diffusely. UA with large leukocytes and patient 
reports discomfort on urinating. Found on CT to have extensive 
fecal loading with RUQ US revealing patent portal vasculature 
with no ascites.

# Abdominal pain- Assessed to be likely due to combination of 
severe constipation and UTI. Patient treated with aggressive 
bowel regimen from above and below and abdominal pain was much 
relieved after passing large bowel movement.  She was discharged 
with additional laxatives to support regular bowel movements. 

#UTI - Patient on admission with large leuk esterace of UA with 
complaints of discomfort on urination. ED report of prurulent 
urine. This may be component of abdominal pain.  There was 
initial concern for pyelonephritis given nausea and vomiting 
though afebrile, no leukocytosis, no CVA tenderness. Still this 
would be covered under current antibiotic regimen.  Patient 
treated with a 7 day course of ciprofloxacin. 

# EtOH cirrhosis- MELD score 11 on admission. transaminases and 
bilirubin nl, INR elevated but seems to be at her baseline of 
1.3-1.5  Patient did not appear encephalopathic on admission but 
did have significant asterixis in all extremities which improved 
after she began stooling.  She also appeared euvolemic on 
admission. She was continued on home diuretic regimen of 
furosemide/aldactone and lactulose TID. 

# Iron deficiency anemia- chronic problem h/h at baseline, 
trended down to low baseline during this admission. Ferrous 
sulfate discontinued as it may be contributing to constipation. 
She was given one dose of IV ferrous gluconate before discharge.

# Coagulopathy- INR 1.5 (baseline 1.3-1.5) Due to chronic 
alcoholic liver disease.

radiology_notes.text: ADDENDUM  THERE IS ALSO TRACE PERIHEPATIC ASCITES.

INDICATION:  ___ with ETOH cirrhosis presents with peritonitis, evaluate for
intra-abdominal process.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT scan of the abdomen and pelvis following the
intravenous administration of 100 cc of Omnipaque in a split bolus .  Coronal
and sagittal reformatted images were also generated for review.

DOSE:  643 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis from ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST:  There is bibasilar dependent atelectasis. The visualized
portions of heart and pericardium are unremarkable. There is no pleural
effusion.  A 1.8 x 0.9 cm right paraspinal nodule is again noted, external to
the lung parenchyma.

LIVER: The liver again demonstrates heterogeneous attenuation and has a
nodular contour compatible with history of cirrhosis. The gallbladder appears
mildly distended without gallbladder wall edema.  There is mild extrahepatic
biliary ductal dilatation, as seen on ultrasound but similar in extent
compared to, prior study. The portal vein is patent. There is mild periportal
edema.

PANCREAS:  The pancreas does not demonstrate focal lesions or peripancreatic
stranding or fluid collection.

SPLEEN:  The spleen is enlarged and measures 14 cm.

ADRENALS:  The adrenal glands are unremarkable.

KIDNEYS:  A 1.3 cm hypodense lesion is again seen in the interpolar region of
the left kidney, unchanged since prior study. The kidneys demonstrate
symmetric nephrograms and excretion of contrast.  No pelvicaliceal dilatation
or perinephric abnormalities are present.

GI TRACT: The stomach is distended with enteric contrast.  The loops of
proximal jejunum and duodenum are borderline prominent without a clear zone of
transition identified. There is some fecalization of the bowel loops. The
appendix is air-filled and normal.

VASCULAR:  The aorta is normal in caliber without aneurysmal dilatation. The
origins of the celiac axis, SMA, bilateral renal arteries, and ___ are patent.

RETROPERITONEUM AND ABDOMEN:  There are scattered prominent mesenteric lymph
nodes around the porta hepatis measuring up to 7 mm in short axis. There is
some low density material surrounding the main portal vein extending into the
root of the mesenteric, likely a reactive process. There are also scattered
prominent retroperitoneal lymph nodes but these are not enlarged by CT size
criteria. No ascites, free air, or abdominal wall hernias are noted.

PELVIC CT:  The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  No
pelvic wall or inguinal lymph node enlargement is seen. There is no pelvic
free fluid.  Fiber uterus is again noted.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No blastic or lytic lesions suspicious for malignancy is
present.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Fecal loading within the colon. Mildly prominent loops of proximal small
bowel without a transition point identified could reflect a focal ileus.

2.  Cirrhotic liver with multiple perfusion abnormalities and splenomegaly.

3.  Stable right perispinal lesion which can be characterize by MRI.

4.  Fibroid uterus.
